claims.statement: app-lynx is the repository's only runtime novel client; the former SolidJS/Capacitor webview client and its novel-reader code were deleted in ADR-0203, with the Android host moved to packages/android-host.

The /novels page renders a single-column native list (list-type=single) feed through createMixFeed with recommend/follow sub-tabs, in-flow restricted novel cards, data-layer AI-only/tag-mute removal, and navigation through the openNovel(id) seam.

Novel entry points route through the openNovel(id) seam, which applies the device-level novel_intro_first setting to emit either /novel/:id/intro or /novel/:id with no route-level redirect (ADR-0167/ADR-0183).

NovelIntro.vue is a cover-scrim decision surface whose restricted/AI masking reuses the body predicates (R18 first, then AI mask) with the same `masked` flag driving handler guards and `:disabled` on every Row-1 control, and whose main CTA switches between start-reading and continue-reading labels through the pure decideIntroReadAction(continueReadingStore.has(novelId)) — defaulting to start-reading while the store's hydrate has not settled — while both branches navigate to the same /novel/:id route.
The intro page builds a narrower export snapshot using caption text and an empty image map because it does not prefetch the novel body.
Novel bookmark and watch-later actions are available from both the intro page and the body page after the object-bound dimension refactor, using BookmarkButton with target-kind=novel.

NovelDetail.vue loads detail first and fetches body text/images only for non-restricted, non-AI novels, with a loadGeneration gate discarding stale responses and restricted novels bypassing the body list entirely.

The novel body is virtualized with a native list (list-type=single) of per-paragraph list-items using stable p-idx keys and estimated heights, plus meta/end/fab-allowance items; ADR-0134 measured deep-scroll jank and memory improvements from this change.

Reading progress uses the main-thread scroll signal via main-thread-bindscroll for the watchlist prompt's ≥70% signal and scrolltolower as the authoritative bottom signal, with a visible warn fallback when the MT signal does not dispatch.

NovelDetail.vue records a session-last continue-reading position on entry with zero threshold (chapter coordinates back-filled afterwards for the 「第N话」 label), and evaluates completion via decideNovelCompletion — behind a content-taller-than-viewport precondition — at bottom, after coordinates land, and after a re-pulled viewport size; a completion is a soft delete (completedAt, which also sweeps the earlier chapters of the same series) and a detail-load failure marks the entry unavailable instead of removing it.

Lynx text selection requires static selection attribute literals, a native clipboard module (there is no navigator/clipboard), and UTF-16 code-unit index snapping; createTextSelection.ts owns event parsing, measurement, placement, dismissal, and copy/search with no optimistic copy success.

The lynx translation stack is a from-scratch BYOK feature (no shared package and no webview reuse) built on a provider-agnostic TranslationProvider whose single OpenAIResponsesProvider maps the OpenAI Responses API events to five TranslationChunk types.

The LLM API key is stored in Android Keystore via the Java PictelioTranslateModule and never enters the JS heap — JS only receives the LlmEndpointPublic mirror, while non-secret baseURL/model/language metadata is persisted in the JS-readable prefs KV and overlaid on that mirror — and native stream delivery uses the pictelioTranslateFrame global event bus (the per-chunk Callback channel is deliberately not used for delivery) with translatePoll retained as a fallback channel carrying the same stamped frames.

createNovelTranslator implements paragraph-boundary chunking at ≤2000 chars, a fixed worker pool (concurrency 3, or 1 on the native bridge), blank-line and [N]-anchor alignment with fallback/overflow reporting, and silent AbortSignal exit.

novelTranslateStore owns the 8-state translation machine, a generation gate and AbortController, a per-chapter in-flight map that reuses the running translation, and a displayParagraphs render source that shows original, translated, or 〔未翻译〕 placeholder text.

Translation cache entries are keyed by novelId|chapterId|targetLang|modelId|sourceHash|baseURLHash with FNV-1a hashes, an LRU cap of 200, only completed chapters written, and a dual adapter: IndexedDB in web-core dev and a native filesystem channel (cacheDir/translations plus manifest.json) in PrimJS.

Translation authorization is independent of content display: isTranslationRestricted aborts R18/R18G requests with a dedicated code before any content leaves the device, while endpoint compatibility (dummy key) and credential verification (real key) are separate persisted states; the body page's translate-entry visibility is a separate display decision (translationEnabled reusing the show-R18 predicates), and blocked requests surface in the UI as aborted rather than failed.

A retryable chunked-pipeline failure triggers one whole-batch fallback (stream=false) with 0ms backoff and isRetryingHint, and partial results render translated paragraphs plus a 〔未翻译〕 placeholder without reporting 100% progress.
@pictelio/novel-export is the zero-DOM single source of truth for the 9-format whitelist, block parsing, HTML extraction, and NovelExportPayload/task-draft construction consumed by app-lynx.

NovelExporter.java is the Java facade that serializes txt/html/md/rtf/json/fb2 inline and delegates epub/docx/pdf to NovelEpubEncoder/NovelDocxEncoder/NovelPdfEncoder, fetching images via PixivImageLoader with bytes never entering JS and outputting through GallerySaver to Downloads/Pictelio.

Novel export is a kind=novel download-queue task whose opaque payloadJson snapshots targetFormat and content switches at enqueue time, reusing the queue's persistence, resume, progress, and share capabilities.

streamId is the shared JS-to-Java key of a translation stream: JS generates it and reuses it as the payload's _abortToken so Java echoes it on every emitted frame, frames carry streamId and a per-stream monotonic seq stamped once on entry into the per-stream buffer, the JS adapter drops frames whose streamId is not the stream's own and dedupes by seq, Java keys its delivery state (STREAM_FRAMES / STREAM_TERMINAL / STREAM_TERMINAL_MSG / STREAM_SEQ) by streamId and prunes other streams when a new one starts, and abort is streamId-direct because the provider registers abortStream(streamId) synchronously instead of waiting for translateStream's promise to settle, with Java marking the id in USER_ABORTED so a user abort is not reported as a failure.

Java's frame attribution is per-stream but its SSE parse state is not: PictelioTranslateModule is a single registered instance whose instance-level sseParser is reassigned and whose single frameQueue is cleared at each stream start, so two overlapping streams can still share parse state even though ADR-0176 decides that the parse state be bucketed per stream alongside the already per-stream delivery maps.

The endpoint probe must send the Responses API-accepted scalar input ("ping"): a bare string array is rejected with 422 by providers such as DeepSeek, and that defect stayed invisible for a dummy key because authentication precedes routing, so a 401/403 verdict proves only that the address accepts and authenticates requests — never that /responses exists; the compatibility chip therefore states only the verified provider/Responses fact and the runtime request path stays unchanged.

Automatic whole-batch fallback is limited to retryable errors, which are exactly server / network / incomplete; the native adapter classifies HTTP status and message into that same subset instead of hardcoding retryable=true, so 429, 401/403, 402, 400, model_not_found, content_filter and endpoint_not_responses never trigger an automatic second request.

The R18/R18G translation authorizations are account-scoped settings keys (settings_translate_r18_${uid} / settings_translate_r18g_${uid}) kept separate from the show_r18_* display keys, with the first enable of each passing an inline risk confirmation in the settings form; isTranslationRestricted(xRestrict) maps xRestrict 1/2 to the corresponding switch and the store refuses the request before it leaves the device.

openNovel(id, opts) is the single novel-navigation seam: it emits /novel/:id/intro or /novel/:id from the pure decideNovelTarget({ novelIntroFirst, resume }) predicate, where the new resume: true intent overrides the novel_intro_first switch and is used only by the continue-reading list — implemented as a parameter on the existing seam rather than a second navigation shortcut.
